correctness.rationale: The q=0 magnetization-layer energy formula, uniform layer separation, strict decreasing-kernel interval inequality, and finite-network Dirichlet star reduction jointly prove the exact limiting mean-time prefactor. Neighbor conductances and the singleton hitting identity are checked with the one-attempt-per-step normalization. The uniform error is justified by fixed N and a uniform gap outside the central layer. The direct checker passes 2,049 finite tests; these are not used in place of the analytical argument.

The 2025 review supplies the motivated metastable prefactor problem and summarizes these results; the 2016 general graph result gives an abstract static prefactor, not this explicit double-scaling shape-gap formula. Targeted mathematical literature comparisons disclosed no covering theorem; implicit prior equivalents remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: At uniform coupling there are C(N,m) critical magnetization configurations whereas every strictly decreasing near-uniform distance kernel has only the two boundary gate minimizers; their ratio is exponentially large with N. The exact beta*q crossover is a natural missing rate calibration for the model rather than an arbitrary finite case. The theorem gives all fixed-N interpolation values and a strict monotonicity law, while respecting the absence of a thermodynamic-limit assertion.
